newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia cuts Lombard rate to 11 from 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia cuts Lombard rate to 11 from 18 pct.

text.p: Croatia's central bank cut the Lombard rate to 11 from 18 percent, it said in a press release on Thursday.
The Lombard rate is regarded as a key lending rate. The discount rate, at 6.5 percent since August, has no practical purpose.
At a meeting on Wednesday afternoon, the bank's board decided to leave the so-called "intervention" or emergency lending rate unchanged at 19 percent in September.
Commercial banks can use intervention loans three times a month for two days to help their liquidity.

Lombard loans are granted for a maximum of 12 days a month using the central bank's bills as a collateral. Until now, the loan volume could total up to 70 percent of the amount of bills each bank had purchased.
In order to ward off inflationary effects of better overall liquidity in the country's banking system, the bank reduced the overall volume of Lombard loans to 50 percent of total bills.
